body.zh-Hant: 克里蒙梭1841年生於旺代，出身共和派、無神論的中產家庭，在第二帝國時期學醫。他於1865至1869年旅居美國。
body.en: Clemenceau was born in 1841 in the Vendée to a bourgeois republican, atheist family and studied medicine under the Second Empire. He lived in the United States from 1865 to 1869.

heading.zh-Hant: 從區長到德雷福斯事件
heading.en: From mayor to the Dreyfus affair

body.zh-Hant: 1870年帝國垮台後，他出任巴黎蒙馬特區區長；1871年3月當選議員，卻因阿爾薩斯—洛林割讓給德國而辭職。1893年因巴拿馬醜聞失去眾議院席位，1902年才以參議員身分重返議會。其間他撰寫大量文章，替德雷福斯平反。
body.en: In 1870, after the fall of the empire, he was named mayor of Montmartre; elected deputy in March 1871, he resigned when Alsace-Lorraine was ceded to Germany. The Panama scandal cost him his seat in 1893, and he returned to parliament only in 1902 as a senator. In between he wrote thousands of articles supporting Dreyfus.

body.zh-Hant: 1906年他以65歲之齡首度入閣，隨後出任總理，任期自1906年到1909年。任內他投入大量精力壓制社會運動，被稱為「破壞罷工者」，因而長期受左派工人憎恨。
body.en: In 1906, aged sixty-five, he became a minister for the first time, then premier from 1906 to 1909. He devoted much of his energy to suppressing social movements, earning the label 'strikebreaker' and the long-lasting hatred of leftist workers.

body.zh-Hant: 一戰期間他拒絕加入神聖同盟政府，主張以意志與決心贏得戰爭。1917年局勢危急，總統普恩加萊勉強請他組閣；自1917年11月16日起，他領導法國走向勝利，聲望極高，但要確保和平則困難得多。
body.en: During the war he refused to join the Sacred Union government and called for will and determination to win. When the situation became critical in 1917, President Poincaré reluctantly called on him to head the government; from 16 November 1917 he led France to victory and became immensely popular, though securing the peace proved far harder.

body.zh-Hant: 1920年他競選共和國總統，希望親自督促《凡爾賽條約》落實，但許多天主教派議員與他在政治生涯中樹立的其他政敵不予支持，他就此退出政壇。此後他旅行與寫作，1922年再赴美國為條約辯護，卻未能說服聽眾。
body.en: In 1920 he ran for president of the Republic, wishing to oversee the enactment of the Treaty of Versailles, but many Catholic politicians and numerous other enemies made during his career withheld their support, and he was removed from political life. He then travelled and wrote, and in 1922 returned to the United States to defend the treaty, but failed to convince.

body.zh-Hant: 蔣介石1887年10月30日生於浙江溪口。1906年赴東京，卻未能取得軍事訓練資格；回國後進保定軍校，之後在東京的士官學校（Shikan Gakko）繼續受軍事教育。在東京由浙江同鄉陳其美介紹加入孫中山的同盟會；1911年10月10日革命在武漢爆發後，他回上海追隨陳其美作戰。
body.en: Chiang was born in Ch'i-k'ou, Chekiang, on 30 October 1887. In 1906 he went to Tokyo but failed to qualify for military training; back in China he studied at the Paoting Military Academy and continued his military education at the Shikan Gakko in Tokyo. In Tokyo his fellow Chekiangese Ch'en Ch'i-mei sponsored his entry into Sun Yat-sen's T'ung-meng hui, and when revolution broke out in Wuhan on 10 October 1911 he returned to Shanghai to fight under Ch'en.

heading.en: Whampoa, the Northern Expedition and Nanking

body.zh-Hant: 1923年蔣介石出任孫中山的參謀長，1924年5月3日起任黃埔軍校校長。1926年7月9日出任北伐軍總司令，並在1927年4月12日對上海的共產黨人與嫌疑者動手清黨；4月18日在南京宣布成立國民政府。北伐第二階段於1928年6月攻克北京，南京成為首都。
body.en: In 1923 Chiang became Sun Yat-sen's chief of staff, and from 3 May 1924 he was commandant of the Whampoa academy. On 9 July 1926 he became supreme commander of the Northern Expedition; on 12 April 1927 he moved against Communists and suspects in Shanghai, and on 18 April proclaimed a national government at Nanking. Peking fell in June 1928 and Nanking became the capital.

body.zh-Hant: 1928至1937年被稱為相對和平的十年。蔣介石在這段期間建立龐大的政治與軍事機器，德國顧問協助建軍，並把共產黨逐出江西根據地。蔣介石也發起新生活運動。1936年12月12日他在西安被張學良扣押，被迫接受聯共抗日，兩週後返回南京。
body.en: The decade from 1928 to 1937 was peaceful only by comparison. Chiang built up a formidable political and military machine, aided by German advisers, which ousted the Communists from Kiangsi, and he launched the New Life Movement. Kidnapped at Sian on 12 December 1936 by Chang Hsüeh-liang, he had to accept a united front against Japan and returned to Nanking a fortnight later.

body.zh-Hant: 抗日戰爭初期，蔣介石的軍隊在上海與南京周邊苦戰，政府先退武漢，1938年底遷重慶。1938年3月他取得「總裁」頭銜，繼孫中山的「總理」。他經羅斯福出面進入大國外交場合，1944年10月促成史迪威被召回。
body.en: In the first year of the Second Sino-Japanese War his armies fought around Shanghai and Nanking, and the government withdrew to Wuhan and then, by the end of 1938, to Chungking. In March 1938 he assumed the title of Tsung-tsai, successor to Sun Yat-sen's Tsung-li. Through Roosevelt he joined the Great Powers' councils, and in October 1944 he secured Stilwell's dismissal.

body.zh-Hant: 戰後國共內戰爆發。1947年1月1日新憲公布，國民大會選蔣介石為總統；1949年1月21日他辭去總統職務，12月10日退往台灣，之後國民大會在台灣再度選他為總統。他於1975年4月5日因心臟病發作去世。
body.en: After the war civil war broke out. A new constitution was promulgated on 1 January 1947 and the National Assembly chose Chiang as president; he retired from the presidency on 21 January 1949 and retired to Taiwan on 10 December 1949, where the National Assembly re-elected him to the presidency. He died of a heart attack on 5 April 1975.

heading.zh-Hant: 出生、流亡與奪回利雅德
heading.en: Birth, exile and the recapture of Riyadh

body.zh-Hant: 伊本·紹德（1880–1953）生於內志的利雅德。1891年隨父親阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼流亡科威特，當時敵對的拉希德家族奪取了紹德家領地。1902年他率少數戰士奇襲奪回利雅德，1913年佔領波斯灣畔的哈薩。
body.en: Ibn Saud (1880–1953) was born in Riyadh in Nejd. In 1891 he went into exile in Kuwait with his father, Abd al-Rahman, after the rival Rashidi family seized Saudi lands. In 1902 he recaptured Riyadh with a small band of warriors, and in 1913 he occupied al-Hasa on the Persian Gulf.

heading.en: Expansion and founding of the kingdom

body.zh-Hant: 1915年他接受英國保護與津貼，條件是不攻擊英國在海灣的利益及麥加的謝里夫侯賽因。1924年他的軍隊圍攻麥加，迫使侯賽因退位流亡；1926年稱漢志國王，次年稱內志國王，1932年兩者合併為沙烏地阿拉伯王國。
body.en: In 1915 he accepted British protection and a subsidy in return for not attacking British interests in the Gulf or Sharif Husein of Mecca. In 1924 his forces besieged Mecca and forced Husein's abdication and exile; in 1926 he took the title king of the Hejaz, a year later that of the Nejd, and in 1932 joined them as the kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

heading.en: The oil era and later years

body.zh-Hant: 1933年他把第一份石油特許權給予後來稱為阿美石油公司的美國公司，但經濟大蕭條與二戰阻礙進一步開發；戰後石油產量與收入迅速成長。他於1953年去世。
body.en: In 1933 he granted the first oil concession to an American company later known as ARAMCO, but the Depression and World War II prevented further development; after the war oil production and revenues grew quickly. He died in 1953.
